questions.question: Bank rate is the rate at which:

options.text: Central Bank borrows loan from Government
Commercial banks lend loan to Central bank
Commercial banks lend loan to Government
Central bank lends loan to commercial banks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Central Bank lends loan to commercial banks.**__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Bank rate:

 
 
• Bank rate is a rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides the loan to commercial banks without keeping any security.
 
• There is no agreement on repurchase that will be drawn up or agreed upon with no collateral as well.
 
• The RBI allows short-term loans with the presence of collateral.
 
• This is known as Repo Rate.
 
• Bank Rates in India is determined by the RBI.
 
• It is usually higher than a Repo Rate on account of its ability to regulate liquidity.
 
• The current Bank Rate is 4.25%.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Monetary Policy:

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (RBI Act) was amended by the Finance Act, 2016, to provide for a statutory and institutionalized framework for a Monetary Policy Committee, for maintaining price stability, while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
 
• The Monetary Policy Committee is entrusted with the task of fixing the benchmark policy rate (repo rate) required to contain inflation within the specified target level.
 
• The Government of India, in consultation with RBI, notified the ‘Inflation Target’ in the Gazette of India dated 5 August 2016 for the period beginning from the date of publication of the notification and ending on March 31, 2021, as 4%.
 
• At the same time, lower and upper tolerance levels were notified to be 2% and 6% respectively.
 
 
 
• Instruments of monetary policy:
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):
 
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio is a specified amount of bank deposits which banks are required to keep with the RBI in the form of reserves or balances.
 
• The higher the CRR with the RBI, the lower will be the liquidity in the system and vice versa.
 
• The CRR was reduced from 15% in 1990 to 5 % in 2002.
 
• The current CRR is 3.00%.
 
 
 
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):
 
 
• All financial institutions have to maintain a certain quantity of liquid assets with themselves at any point in time of their total time and demand liabilities.
 
• This is known as the Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
 
• The assets are kept in non-cash forms such as precious metals, bonds, etc.
 
• The current percentage of SLR is 18%.
 
 
 
• Bank Rate Policy:
 
 
• Also known as the discount rate, bank rates are interest charged by the RBI for providing funds and loans to the banking system.
 
• An increase in bank rate increases the cost of borrowing by commercial banks which results in the reduction in credit volume to the banks and hence the supply of money declines.
 
• An increase in the bank rate is the symbol of the tightening of the RBI monetary policy.
 
• The current Bank Rate is 4.25%.

questions.question: All monetary transfers or kinds sent by migrants to their place of origin are called ______.

The correct answer is __**remittances**__.

__
 
• **Remittances:**

 
 
• **Remittances are usually understood as financial or in-kind transfers made by migrants to friends and relatives back in communities of origin.**
 
• These are the sum of **two main components:**
 
• Personal Transfers in cash or in-kind between resident and non-resident households and Compensation of Employees, which refers to the income of workers who work in another country for a limited period.
 
• Remittances help in stimulating economic development in recipient countries, but this can also make such countries over-reliant on them.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• India is followed by **China, Mexico, the Philippines, and Egypt.**
 
• **The United States is the biggest source**, accounting for over 20% of all Remittances.

questions.question: The number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period is called the _______

__
 
• The velocity of money **refers to how often one unit of currency is used for purchases in a given time period.**
 
• It's calculated by dividing the** nominal GDP by the total amount of money supply.**
 
• High velocity indicates a **healthy economy and low velocity can indicate a sluggish economy.**
 
• Understanding the velocity of money assists central banks in formulating monetary policy.
 
• **High velocity can sometimes be associated with inflation, though the relationship is complex.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• **Remittances:** These are funds transferred by **migrant workers back to their home country, playing a crucial role in the economies of many developing countries.**
 
• **Zero Economic Profit: **It occurs when a** firm's total revenues are exactly equal to its total opportunity costs, including both explicit and implicit costs, meaning the firm is just covering all its costs but not making any surplus profits.**

• The reverse repo rate is the rate of interest at which the RBI borrows funds from other banks in the short term.

questions.question: _________ refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Open Market Operations.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)** are the actions taken by a central bank to buy or sell government bonds in the open market.
 
• This process is used **to regulate the money supply** and influence interest rates in the economy.
 
• When the central bank buys bonds, it increases the money supply, making it easier for banks to lend money and potentially lowering interest rates.
 
• Conversely, **when it sells bonds, it decreases the money supply**, which can lead to higher interest rates.
 
• OMOs are a primary tool for monetary policy and are critical in managing economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Requirement:**

 
 
• Marginal requirement refers to the **minimum percentage of deposits** that banks are required to keep as reserves.
 
• It is not directly related to the buying or selling of government bonds.
 
• This requirement is set by the central bank and is** aimed at ensuring that banks maintain liquidity**.
 
• Changes in marginal requirements can affect the money supply and lending capacity of banks.
 
 
 
• **Closed Market Operations:**
 
 
• Closed Market Operations are not a standard term in monetary policy and typically** refer to scenarios where a central bank does not engage **in buying or selling government securities.
 
• It can** also imply a market **where there are **restrictions on the buying and selling **of government bonds.
 
• This term is less commonly used compared to open market operations.
 
 
 
• **Moral Suasion:**
 
 
• Moral suasion is a** non-coercive method used by central banks** to persuade banks and financial institutions to adhere to certain policies.
 
• It involves **communication and appeals** rather than direct action, such as buying or selling bonds.
 
• While it can influence monetary policy, it does not involve the actual trading of government bonds in the market.
 
• This approach** relies on the credibility of the central bank **to guide the financial behavior of institutions.

questions.question: Which of the following unemployment types is the result of people voluntarily leaving jobs in search of better ones?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frictional unemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Frictional unemployment occurs when individuals voluntarily leave their jobs to find better opportunities or jobs that are a better fit for their skills.
 
• This type of unemployment is usually short-term and is a natural part of the job market.
 
• It can be beneficial as it allows workers to find positions where they can be more productive and satisfied.
 
• Frictional unemployment is often influenced by factors such as job search time, availability of information about job vacancies, and mobility of labor.
 
• It is different from other types of unemployment as it is not caused by economic downturns or structural changes in the economy but by individual choices and job transitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disguised Unemployment**

 
 
• Occurs when more people are employed than actually needed, leading to low productivity.
 
• Common in agricultural and informal sectors where surplus labor doesn't contribute to additional output.
 
 
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment**
 
 
• Results from economic downturns and is linked to the business cycle.
 
• Increases during recessions and decreases during periods of economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Structural Unemployment**
 
 
• Caused by changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or shifts in consumer demand.
 
• Workers' skills may no longer match the job requirements, leading to longer periods of unemployment.

questions.question: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phillips curve**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Phillips curve** examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes.
 
• It suggests that there is an inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.
 
• The curve was introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958, based on empirical data from the United Kingdom.
 
• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy is associated with higher rates of wage inflation.
 
• Conversely, higher unemployment is associated with lower rates of wage inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indifference Curve**

 
 
• Can be caused by **changes in consumer preferences, income levels, prices of related goods, and more**. A rightward shift indicates an increase in demand, while a leftward shift indicates a decrease.
 
• An indifference curve represents a graph showing different combinations of two goods that provide the same level of satisfaction or utility to a consumer
 
• Indicates that as a consumer consumes more of one good, they must consume less of the other to maintain the same utility level.
 
• Reflects the diminishing marginal rate of substitution; consumers are willing to give up fewer units of one good to obtain additional units of another good as they have more of it.
 
• Curves that are further from the origin represent higher levels of satisfaction.
 
 
 
• **Supply Curve**
 
 
• A supply curve illustrates the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity of that good that producers are willing to supply.
 
• Indicates that as prices increase, suppliers are willing to offer more of the good, reflecting the profit motive.
 
• Can occur due to factors such as changes in production costs, technology, or number of suppliers. A rightward shift indicates an increase in supply, while a leftward shift indicates a decrease.
 
 
 
• ** Demand Curve**
 
 
• A demand curve shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded by consumers.
 
• Reflects the law of demand, which states that as prices decrease, the quantity demanded increases, and vice versa.

questions.question: Which of the following age groups is considered as working population or working age in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15-59 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The working age population in India is generally considered to be those aged between **15 and 59 years**.
 
• This age group is crucial as they are actively involved in the workforce and contribute significantly to the economic development of the country.
 
• Policies and programs aimed at employment, skill development, and social security are primarily targeted towards individuals within this age bracket.
 
• National policies, such as the National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, focus on this age group to enhance their employability and productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demographic Dividend:**

 
 
• The demographic dividend refers to the economic growth potential that can result from shifts in a population’s age structure, mainly when the share of the working-age population is larger than the non-working-age population.
 
• India is expected to have a demographic dividend advantage until around 2055.
 
• Effective policies and investments in health, education, and employment are essential to maximize the benefits of the demographic dividend.
 
 
 
• **Skill India Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, the mission aims to train over 40 crore people in different skills by 2022.
 
• It includes various initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the National Skill Development Mission.
 
 
 
• **Employment Generation Programs:**
 
 
• Programs like Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provide wage employment opportunities to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.
 
• Start-Up India and Stand-Up India schemes aim to promote entrepreneurship and job creation.
 
 
 
• **Social Security Schemes:**
 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) provides old age protection and social security to unorganized workers.
 
• Atal Pension Yojana (APY) aims to create a universal social security system for all Indians, especially the poor, the underprivileged, and the workers in the unorganized sector.

questions.question: The central bank may ________ to discourage credit in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase bank rate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The bank rate** is the interest rate at which the central bank **lends money** to commercial banks.
 
• When the central bank** increases the bank rate**, it becomes **more expensive** for commercial banks to borrow money from the central bank.
 
• This, in turn,** reduces** the amount of credit that commercial banks can offer to their customers, thereby **discouraging credit** in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Increasing **the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is another tool that the central bank can use to** discourage credit.**

 
 
• **CRR **is the amount of funds that commercial banks have to keep with the central bank as a** percentage of their deposits**.
 
• When the **CRR is decreased**, banks have more funds available to lend, which can lead to an** increase in credit** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Buying securities** in the open market is a tool that the central bank can use to **increase liquidity** in the economy.
 
 
• When the central bank buys securities, it i**njects money** into the economy, which can lead to an** increase in credit.**
 
• Therefore, this option is** not** suitable for discouraging credit in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Reducing** the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio** (SLR) is another tool that the central bank can use to **increase the availability of funds** for banks to lend.
 
 
• SLR is the percentage of deposits that banks have to keep in the form of liquid assets such as** cash, gold, or government securities.**
 
• When the SLR is** reduced**, banks have** more funds available** to lend, which can lead to an increase in credit in the economy.

questions.question: In India, inflation is measured on the basis of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Consumer price index.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inflation** refers to the rise in the average price level of goods and services leading to a decline in the value of money within a particular economy.
 
• The wholesale price index and the consumer price index are the two main indicators of inflation in India.
 
• The wholesale price index is considered as the primary inflation measure in India.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India had adopted the **consumer price index as its key measure of inflation in India** since 2014.
 
• **The consumer price index** is the measure of the average change over time in the prices of consumer goods and services purchased by households.
 
 
• The percentage change in the consumer price index over a period of time gives the amount of inflation over that specific period.
 
• Consumer Price Index in India is published by the Central Statistical Organization (CSO).
 
• It is published monthly in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Wholesale Price Index** measures the average change in the prices of commodities for bulk sale at the level of the early stage of transactions.

 
 
• Countries like the Philippines use wholesale price index changes as a central measure of inflation.
 
• The wholesale price index is published by the office of economic adviser, ministry of commerce and industry.
 
 
 
• **The Producer Price Index **is the measure of the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers of goods and services.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about unemployment in India:

a) Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in urban areas.

b) Educated unemployed people are mainly found in rural areas of India.

c) Higher cropping intensity is desirable for reducing unemployment in the rural economy.

Which of the given statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only c**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct choice is: c)** Higher cropping intensity (greater number of crops grown in a year on the same land) can indeed help reduce unemployment in rural areas by providing more continuous work for agricultural laborers.Higher cropping intensity (greater number of crops grown in a year on the same land) can indeed help reduce unemployment in rural areas by providing more continuous work for agricultural laborers.
 
• The given statements **a) and b) are typically incorrect **based on the general understanding of these terms:
 
 
• a) Seasonal Unemployment is primarily found in agriculture-dominated rural areas, not urban areas. This is because agriculture in India is largely dependent on the monsoon season, creating periods of high activity and low activity.
 
• b) Educated unemployment, or a situation where educated individuals are unable to find suitable jobs, is typically associated with urban areas rather than rural areas. This is due to higher access to education in urban regions and the propensity for educated individuals to look for employment in urbanized, industrial, or service-based sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Unemployment**: This type of unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills possessed by job seekers and the skills demanded by employers. It often results from changes in technology or shifts in the economy, leaving some workers with obsolete skills.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment**: Frictional unemployment refers to the temporary period of unemployment that arises when individuals are transitioning between jobs or entering the workforce for the first time. It's often considered natural as people search for better opportunities.
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment**: This type of unemployment is linked to the business cycle. It occurs when economic downturns lead to reduced demand for goods and services, resulting in reduced production and layoffs. As the economy improves, this type of unemployment tends to decrease.
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**: Seasonal unemployment arises due to the seasonal nature of certain industries. Workers in agriculture, tourism, and other sectors experience joblessness during off-peak seasons when demand for their services declines.
 
• **Disguised Unemployment**: This situation occurs when more people are engaged in a task or job than actually required, leading to inefficiencies and reduced productivity. It's often seen in rural areas where multiple family members work on a farm but could be replaced by fewer workers using modern techniques.
 
• **Educational Unemployment**: This is when individuals are unemployed due to the lack of necessary education or skills required for available jobs. It highlights the importance of aligning education and training with the demands of the job market.
 
• **Underemployment**: Underemployment refers to a situation where workers are employed in jobs that are below their skill levels or that don't utilize their full capabilities. This often leads to lower income and job dissatisfaction.

• By serving as a store of value, unit of account, and medium of exchange, money simplifies and enhances economic transactions.

• The addition to the capital stock in an economy is measured by net investment or new capital formation, which is expressed as

• In other words, gross investment is the amount that a company has invested in particular assets or the business as a whole without considering depreciation for the same.
 
 
 
• Net Investment, on the other hand, is the actual addition that is made to the capital stock in a given period.
 
 
• Net Investment takes into account the depreciation and is calculated by subtracting the depreciation from the gross investment.

• It refers to the GDP at the current market prices i.e., the GDP is calculated as per the market prices for the year for which the GDP is calculated.
 
 
 
• Real GDP:
 
 
• It refers to the GDP at base year prices i.e., the GDP is calculated as per the market prices in the base year. Thus, the Real GDP negates the inflation in goods and services.

questions.question: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?

__
 
• Fisher's equation of exchange is represented as **MV=PT**.
 
• In this equation, **M** stands for the money supply in an economy.
 
• **V** represents the velocity of money, which is the rate at which money circulates in the economy.
 
• **P** is the price level, and **T** represents the total volume of transactions.

• **Money Supply (M)**

 
 
• The total amount of monetary assets available in an economy at a specific time.
 
• It includes various components such as currency in circulation and demand deposits.
 
• Changes in the money supply can influence inflation, interest rates, and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Velocity of Money (V)**
 
 
• The rate at which money is exchanged from one transaction to another.
 
• It indicates the efficiency of money in an economy; a higher velocity means money is changing hands more frequently.
 
• Velocity is calculated as the ratio of nominal GDP to the money supply.
 
 
 
• **Price Level (P)**
 
 
• The average of current prices across the entire spectrum of goods and services produced in the economy.
 
• It is often measured by price indices such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) or the GDP deflator.
 
• Changes in the price level reflect inflation or deflation in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Total Volume of Transactions (T)**
 
 
• The total number of transactions or the total quantity of goods and services traded in the economy.
 
• This can include consumer spending, business investments, and government expenditures.
 
• The volume of transactions is an indicator of economic activity.

questions.question: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Philips curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Philips curve represents the inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.
 
• The concept was first introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958.
 
• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy leads to higher wages, which in turn leads to higher inflation.
 
• This relationship suggests that policymakers face a trade-off between reducing unemployment and controlling inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Friedman's Model**

 
 
• Also known as the Monetarist Theory, it was proposed by Milton Friedman.
 
• Friedman argued that there is no long-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment, as suggested by the Phillips curve.
 
• He introduced the concept of the Natural Rate of Unemployment, which posits that the economy will always revert to this natural rate despite short-term fluctuations.
 
• Friedman emphasized the role of monetary policy in controlling inflation.
 
 
 
• **Keynesian Model**
 
 
• Developed by John Maynard Keynes, this model emphasizes total spending in the economy (aggregate demand) and its effects on output and inflation.
 
• Keynesians advocate for active government intervention to manage economic cycles.
 
• They believe that insufficient demand can lead to prolonged periods of high unemployment.
 
• In contrast to the Phillips curve, Keynesians may support policies that increase aggregate demand to reduce unemployment without necessarily causing high inflation.
 
 
 
• **Baumol Hypothesis**
 
 
• Proposed by economist William J. Baumol, it addresses the cost disease in service sectors.
 
• Baumol's hypothesis suggests that wages in labor-intensive sectors (like services) rise due to wage increases in other sectors that experience higher productivity growth.
 
• This leads to higher costs in the service sector without corresponding increases in productivity.
 
• The hypothesis is often used to explain rising costs in sectors such as healthcare and education.

questions.question: Money multiplier uses which of the following monetary instruments for its calculation?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Cash reserve ratio (CRR) is the percentage of deposits that commercial banks are required to keep with the central bank as a reserve. It is a monetary policy tool used by central banks to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• The money multiplier is calculated by dividing the total amount of deposits by the cash reserve ratio. This means that the higher the cash reserve ratio, the lower the money multiplier, and vice versa.

questions.question: Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in the economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proportional income tax**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proportional income tax** can act as an **automatic stabilizer in the economy because it changes in response to changes in income levels.**
 
• This means that as** income levels rise or fall, the tax burden for individuals and households changes proportionally,** which can help to stabilize the economy during periods of economic growth or recession.
 
• During periods of **economic growth, when income levels rise, the government collects more revenue from income taxes.**
 
• This increased revenue can be used to fund government spending programs or to** reduce the budget deficit.**
 
• The **government **can also use this **increased revenue to reduce taxes or to provide tax incentives, which can further stimulate economic growth.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Professional tax**

 
 
• **​ **is a tax levied by some state governments in India on individuals who earn an **income through professions, trades, callings or employment.**
 
• It is a form of tax that is collected by the **state government, and the rates and rules may vary from state to state. **
 
• The **professional tax** is usually** deducted by the employer from the salary of the employee and then remitted to the state government.**
 
• The amount of professional tax that an individual has to pay** depends on the monthly or annual income earned, as well as the state in which the individual is employed.**
 
• The purpose of the professional tax is to** help state governments generate revenue for their various development projects and public services.**
 
• It is a **mandatory tax** that must be **paid by individuals who are liable to pay it, and failure to do so can result in penalties and fines.**
 
 
 
• **Wealth tax:**
 
 
• **​**A** tax on an individual's net wealth or assets.**
 
• A form of direct taxation aimed at reducing wealth inequality.
 
• Levied annually based on the value of an individual's assets at a particular point in time.
 
• Can be applied to a range of assets **including cash, property, investments, and personal possessions.**
 
• The** tax rate is usually a percentage of the net value of these assets** and **can vary depending on the level of wealth.**
 
• Used by some countries to generate revenue and fund public services
 
 
 
• **Capital gains tax:****​**
 
 
• Capital gains tax is a tax on the profit earned from the sale of an **asset, such as stocks, real estate, or artwork.**
 
• It is a form of **direct tax that is imposed by the government on the capital gains** realized by an individual or a business.
 
• When a person or a business sells an asset, the **capital gain is the difference between the selling price of the asset and the purchase price or the cost basis of the asset.**
 
• The** capital gains tax is then calculated based on the capital gain realized.**
 
• The capital gains tax rate can vary depending on the asset, the length of time the asset was held, and the taxpayer's income level.

• Money also acts as a **measure of value**, i.e., it helps in determining the value of goods and services.
 
 
 
• The secondary functions of money include acting as a** store of value**, i.e., it helps in storing the wealth in the form of money.

• The contingent functions of money include acting as a means of **distribution of national income**, i.e., it helps in distributing the national income among various sections of the society.
